title: SpaceX shares resume recent decline after one-session respite
Tesla earnings: Stock drops 3% after EV maker delivers revenue beat but big profit miss
content: : Michael Siluk/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images Tesla stock slipped more than 3% in after hours trading after the EV maker delivered revenue ahead of estimates but adjusted earnings per share that missed Wall Street's expectations. Tesla delivered $28.24 billion in revenue in the second quarter, topping analysts' estimates of $26.31 billion. Quarterly profit was far less than anticipated, with adjusted EPS of 33 cents compared to estimates of 50 cents. "Q2 was a strong quarter for our core vehicle, energy and services businesses as well as our manufacturing, infrastructure and AI initiatives," the company said in its earnings release. The second-quarter report is Tesla's first since Elon Musk's other big company went public last month . Expect analysts on the call to press Musk for answers on a potential SpaceX-Tesla merger . Bulls say that a tie-up of the two companies is a natural fit and would streamline some of Musk's goals . Otherwise, the call will be an important update on the big ideas that Tesla has been trying to sell Wall Street on for years now, mainly robotaxis and humanoid robots, or "physical AI." Tesla stock is down about 14% year to date. Tesla's call with analysts will begin around 5:30 p.m. ET. Follow along for the latest: Want a Roadster? Please hold! (Again.) Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveils the Roadster 2 during a presentation in Hawthorne, California Thomson Reuters Tesla's long-suffering second-generation Roadster is still in "design development," the company reported on Wednesday — it's had that designation for about 9 years. The first iteration of the Roadster was Tesla's first vehicle. Essentially a Lotus Elise with a Tesla battery bolted on, it was key to Tesla's initial branding success, making the case that electric vehicles could also be sporty. Musk said in late 2017 that the company would launch a refreshed version and started collecting deposits on the car. But it has remained in development limbo since. Musk has teased a demo for some point this year. Tesla's automotive revenue grew 23% year over year. Tesla recorded $20.52 billion in vehicle sales, handedly beating Wall Street's estimates of $18.68 billion. Tesla made money on its SpaceX investment Tesla revealed a roughly $1 billion unrealized gain on its existing SpaceX investment. Last quarter, the company said it purchased $2 billion worth of stock in the joint AI and space technology company. Tesla's Q2 earnings are out — see the key numbers Revenue: $28.24 billion vs. $26.31 billion estimate Adjusted EPS: 33c vs. 50c estimate Gross margin : 16.8% vs. 19.4% estimate Capital expenditures: $5.79 billion vs. $6.59 billion estimate A bot for home chores? CEO Elon Musk is taking Tesla on a major pivot away from traditional auto sales and into AI-led products. Its most notable product, the Optimus humanoid robot, is racing toward its promised delivery date. During Tesla's April earnings call, Musk said low-volume production of the latest Optimus robot would begin in Fremont in late July or August. Tesla has released several videos of the factory rebuild on X. Investors will be looking for updates on production during Wednesday's call. The Tesla Diner just turned one AaronP/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images Tesla's diner just blew the candles out on its one-year-old birthday. The spaceship-shaped, Los Angeles-based diner with a line of fast-charging ports first opened on July 21, 2025. Tesla says it has since supported 580,000 charging sessions, something that Max de Zegher, the company's senior director of charging, called the "highest usage Supercharger in the world." The diner is now serving a new hot dog drizzled with American cheese and topped with potato sticks, called the "Launch Dog." It's served in a cardboard box that's shaped like a rocket ship. The diner might get some sister restaurants. On X, Musk has teased that there are "more to come." Tesla's energy-storage business had another enormous quarter Tesla's energy business came roaring back. On July 2, the company reported deploying 13.5 GWh of energy storage products, a 53.4% increase compared to the first quarter of 2026. Still, it came in nearly 5% lower than its peak power deployment in the final quarter of 2025. Tesla's energy business is increasingly important to Musk's company: it has higher margins than its automotive sales and helps power SpaceX and Meta's data centers. Whispers about a SpaceX merger grow Spencer Platt/Getty Images Tesla has been somewhat overshadowed recently by another corner of Elon Musk's business empire. SpaceX, Musk's rocket company/AI lab/social media meme feed, raised $86 billion in a record-breaking public listing last month and quickly eclipsed Tesla by rocketing to a $2 trillion-plus market cap. SpaceX has come back down to earth in recent weeks with a major share price fall, but the rocket maker — which also counts Musk as its CEO — is still worth nearly $200 billion more than Tesla. The buzz around SpaceX has fuelled rumors that Musk might merge the two companies. A potential tie-up with SpaceX was one of the most-discussed topics on the online forum for Tesla shareholders to submit questions to executives ahead of earnings. Robotaxi ramps up… but slower than predicted Elon Musk has made grand predictions about Tesla's robotaxi service. So far, they've largely been wide of the mark. A year on from the billionaire's prediction that Tesla's driverless taxis would be serving half the US population by the end of 2025, the company is still some way from hitting that milestone. Tesla announced on Tuesday that robotaxi operations had begun in Orlando and Tampa, following the launch of small-scale services in Miami and three Texan cities. However, with the company pumping billions into AI and autonomy, analysts and investors want to see results. "Strong auto and energy deliveries set Tesla up for a solid quarter, but we believe the key investor debate remains unchanged: can Robotaxi and Optimus progress quickly enough to justify an accelerating AI investment cycle?" analysts from Morgan Stanley wrote in a July 13 note. Tesla's EV business bounces back Cheng Xin/Getty Images After a rocky 2025, Tesla's global electric vehicle business is heading in the right direction again. The Model Y maker reported booming second-quarter sales earlier this month, with EV deliveries rising 25% year-over-year, thanks in part to high gas prices. The surge suggested that Tesla has largely recovered from last year's sales slump, which was partially driven by the end of the $7,500 tax credit for new electric vehicles. Wall Street was unimpressed by the rosy sales figures, with Tesla's stock falling as much as 8% after the numbers dropped. Despite the company's vehicle business recovering, Elon Musk has made it clear that Tesla's future lies in robotaxis and humanoid robots , not EVs. Cantor's bullish target rooted in Tesla's robotaxi business Cantor Fitzgerald has a $510 price target for Tesla stock, 35% higher than Wednesday's price. Analyst Andres Sheppard highlighted the latest vehicle deliveries beat and successful robotaxi rollout, noting that his team expects to see progress continue. "Overall, we continue to see Tesla's Robotaxi segment and Cybercab as a software-as-a-service, high-margin model," he noted. "We continue to expect TSLA will have the ability to scale rapidly following commercialization (despite the delayed expansion) and capture meaningful market share." Auto revenues are increasingly irrelevant for the stock, Barclays says STR/NurPhoto via Getty Images Barclays is less bullish on Tesla stock than some Wall Street peers, maintaining a $370 price target and equal weight rating. While its analysts noted that the company's automotive business is improving, they raised the question of how much that actually matters going forward. "We believe the key message from the market with respect to Tesla's frothy multiple has been that Tesla's current revenue stream (which is predominantly automotive) is increasingly irrelevant, with the key focus for the stock on future mega-growth initiatives in AI - Robotaxi /FSD / autonomous driving + bots / Optimus humanoids," Barclays wrote. "Physical AI" will require significant capex Analysts at Oppenheimer say that Tesla's transition to a leader in "physical AI" will require substantial capex to acquire the necessary compute power and memory capacity. "We anticipate investors will begin looking at capital investments as a leading indicator of Physical AI success," Oppenheimer analysts wrote." The firm recently raised its capex outlook for Tesla from $18 billion to $20 billion for the year as it predicts Tesla to "aggressively bring capacity online to enable AI-driven learning cycles on product design, manufacturing processes, and software integration in to products." Narrative updates won't be enough to drive "decisive" shift for the stock, MS says Sjoerd van der Wal/Getty Images Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco expects to see progress on several key fronts, though he says the report in unlikely to deliver a significant narrative update to spur a new burst of gains for the stock. "Strong auto and energy deliveries improve near-term fundamentals, but we continue to believe Robotaxi and Optimus will be the primary drivers for the stock," he said. "Into earnings we expect constructive updates across both, though likely not enough to drive a decisive re-rating." Tesla heads into earnings with "bears in control" According to data from S3 Partners, short interest in Tesla stock has spiked since the end of March, rising from 60 million shares to 80 million. "The steady increase suggests bearish conviction has continued to build heading into earnings. Rather than reducing exposure ahead of a potentially volatile catalyst, short positioning has continued to build alongside weakening price action ," S3 managing director, Matthew Unterman, wrote on Tuesday. From a technical perspective, shares have fallen below their 50-day and 200-day moving averages. Both are now overhead resistance levels for the stock, S3 said. BofA says focus to be on robotaxi deployment Bloomberg/Getty Images BofA rates Tesla stock as a "Buy" ahead of earnings and maintains a $391 price target, slightly higher than Wednesday's price. The bank's analysts see the rollout of Tesla robotaxis and Optimus humanoid robot production as key points of interest. "We think focus for earnings will remain on TSLA's robotaxi deployments," BofA wrote. "TSLA added an additional market & is scaling TX fleet. We think core auto business remains healthy with reported 2Q deliveries above Street as TSLA gains global BEV market share." title: Prediction: In 5 Years, This Will Be Netflix's Biggest Rival
content: Key Points Netflix has been adding podcasts and more content from popular creators. It may be preparing itself for a much more intense rivalry with YouTube in the future. 10 stocks we like better than Netflix › Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) has been evolving its business over the years by adding live sports, podcasts, and even games. Its subscriptions now offer a wider range of entertainment options, and they've proven superior to other streaming services, enabling the business to grow while also commanding strong profit margins. But its largest rivalry may still be in its early stages, and it's one even my kids see coming. Netflix may be on a collision course with YouTube. Here's why I think it'll be far and away its biggest rival in five years. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Image source: Netflix. Netflix has been adding content from popular creators In what appears to be a more concerted effort to attract traffic from YouTube, which is owned by Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL), Netflix has been adding content from creators such as Ms. Rachel, Mark Rober, and many others. The first season of Ms. Rachel generated 37 million views in the first six months of the year, according to Netflix's data, and ranked as the ninth-most-watched show during that period. Not only is bringing in more content creators on Netflix's platform a more cost-effective option for the streaming company than producing its own shows, but it can also quickly add a wider range of content to its platform to drive more growth. Between bringing on more creators and adding podcasts, Netflix may already be preparing for a much bigger battle brewing ahead with YouTube. The challenge will be that, since YouTube is accessible without a paid subscription, Netflix will need to convince viewers that comparable content is worth paying for. One option, however, could be that the streaming company drastically changes its strategy and, like YouTube, begins to offer content without a subscription, relying entirely on ads. This could be Netflix's biggest challenge yet YouTube has a huge advantage given the sheer breadth and depth of its offerings. Not only is there a wide range of content available on its platform, but it's also more convenient for people who don't want to watch long shows or movies but still want something longer than just a short. And with Netflix raising its prices over the years, it may not offer the same enticing value it once did. Netflix may not be doomed, but it may be facing its most formidable rival yet in YouTube. Alphabet is a tech giant with the deep pockets and resources necessary to back YouTube's continued growth, as it has also been expanding into live sports. This year, Netflix's stock is struggling, and although I still think it can do well in the long run, investors are right to be at least somewhat worried about its future. title: What to Do With a $5 Million Inheritance
content: Inheriting $5 million can be a tremendous financial opportunity, but financial planning is still important. With more assets and tax considerations to take into account, it can help to plan ahead. As a result, understanding what you've inherited and how you might minimize tax consequences may have as much of an impact on your wealth as investing right away. Do you have questions about how to handle a windfall? Speak with a financial advisor today. Understand What You Inherited A $5 million inheritance is rarely a single check. More likely, it's a mix of assets, each with their own rules for taxes, liquidity and long-term planning. Before making any financial decisions, it can help to create a complete inventory of what you've inherited, and identify how each asset is titled. This can help when it comes time to determine whether it's subject to distribution rules and what type of tax treatment applies. Because larger estates tend to be more complex, it's common to inherit several asset types at once. Understanding each one separately can potentially help you minimize mistakes and prioritize the most immediate decisions. With a larger inheritance , the challenge is often less about choosing investments and more about coordinating multiple asset types with different tax rules and timelines. Taking inventory first help build the foundation for every decision that follows. Accounting for Taxes One mistake heirs may make is assuming all inherited assets are taxed the same way. With a $5 million inheritance, that misconception can become especially expensive. Here's what you need to know about the taxes for each type of asset that you might inherit: Story Continues SmartAsset and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below. Because the tax rules for inherited retirement accounts are complex, and vary depending on factors such as your relationship to the deceased and whether required minimum distributions apply, a thoughtful withdrawal strategy can make a substantial difference in how much of the inheritance you ultimately keep. Planning for the Future Once you've accounted for taxes and understand what you've inherited, the next step is deciding how the assets fit into your financial plan. You may want to start by setting aside enough cash for any near-term expenses, taxes or planned purchases. From there, your investment strategy could reflect your time horizon and long-term goals, rather than the emotions that often accompany a large inheritance. A financial advisor can help you build a tax plan. Speak with an advisor today. While a $5 million estate is generally below the current federal estate tax exemption , some states impose their own estate or inheritance taxes with much lower thresholds. Depending on where you live and where inherited assets are located, those rules may influence future planning decisions. The goal isn't simply to invest the inheritance; it's to organize it into a coordinated strategy that supports your priorities while accounting for taxes, liquidity, long-term wealth preservation and more. Working with a financial advisor and tax professional can help you coordinate complex assets, reduce taxes and build a strategy that preserves your inheritance for years to come. title: Why Supermicro Stock Is Surging Even as Revenue Falls Short
content: Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ: SMCI ) gave investors conflicting figures in its Q4 preliminary update on July 21. Fiscal Q4 revenue is expected near the bottom of its $11 billion to $12.5 billion guidance, below the $11.67 billion analyst consensus, yet shares jumped 17.5% after hours. Our take is that the market was not celebrating sales; rather, it was repricing how much profit Supermicro might extract from them. The Margin Surprise Changes the Quarter Supermicro now expects both GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins of 15% to 17%, almost twice its previous 8.2% to 8.4% forecast. At $11 billion of revenue, the new range implies roughly $1.65 billion to $1.87 billion of gross profit, compared with $902 million to $924 million under the old forecast. Even the low end of the new range exceeds the high end of the old one by about $726 million. The reversal follows gross margins of only 6.3% in fiscal Q2 and 9.9% in Q3. Management attributed it to favorable customer and product mix. That can explain one quarter, but not yet a durable change. Mix can reverse quickly. Why Supermicro Stock Is Surging Even as Revenue Falls Short Copyright: ralwel / 123RF Stock Photo Record Orders Raise the Execution Stakes Supermicro received more than $60 billion of new orders during fiscal Q4 and ended the year with record backlog. The orders are expected to ship over future quarters, giving the company strong demand visibility despite revenue landing near the bottom of its current-quarter guidance. Supermicro's immediate challenge would be converting high demand into revenue without sacrificing its improved margins. The gap between orders and recognized revenue remains critical. In June, Supermicro announced $7 billion of equity and equity-linked financing to buy components for roughly $39 billion of AI-server orders from more than 20 customers. Demand may be abundant, but filling it consumes working capital and can dilute existing shareholders. A Fundamental Rerating With a Squeeze Attached Long and short sentiment are sharply split. Insider Monkey counted 49 hedge funds holding Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI) at the end of Q1. Meanwhile, 103.2 million shares were sold short as of June 30, roughly one-fifth of the float and 7.2% above the previous report. That positioning probably amplified the rally. However, a 1.6-day short-interest ratio means SMCI trades heavily enough to prevent a classic prolonged squeeze. The margin surprise is pretty substantial, not just mechanical. The August 11 results are the real test. If 15% to 17% margins persist, Supermicro's earnings power has changed. If margins drift back toward 10%, the surge will look more like relief and short covering than a durable rerating. title: Top NATO general says he believes alliance forces are ready for a drone-infested battlefield like the one in Ukraine
content: NATO's top general said Western forces could survive a battlefield like the one in Ukraine. Ben Birchall/PA Images via Getty Images NATO's top general said allied forces could survive a battlefield like the one in Ukraine. The front lines in that war are dominated by drones, electronic warfare, and constant surveillance. Gen. Alexus Grynkewich said Ukraine's participation in NATO exercises has helped the alliance. NATO's top general said that he believes allied forces could survive on a battlefield like the one in Ukraine , saturated with drones, electronic warfare, and constant surveillance. "I think the answer is we're ready for that," US Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe , told Business Insider at the Farnborough International Airshow in England this week, offering fresh reassurance at a time when warfare is changing rapidly. Grynkewich, one of NATO's two strategic commanders, oversees the alliance's military operations . He said that forces across Europe are training to operate in environments like the one in Ukraine. "We are learning every single day from the Ukrainians — how they're dealing with this," Grynkewich said. "And the technology and tactics are, frankly, evolving really fast. So it's kind of persistent contact that we have to have with those on the front line, so we can understand," he added. The front line stretching across southern and eastern Ukraine has evolved into what soldiers and officials describe as a wide "kill zone" that extends 10 to 20 kilometers from the line of contact, sometimes farther in certain places. The zone is heavily saturated with drones constantly monitoring the battlefield below, capable of targeting both soldiers and vehicles. Any movement can trigger a deadly, pinpoint strike. The kill zone in Ukraine is overwhelmed with drones constantly watching for any movement. Dmytro Smolienko/Ukrinform/NurPhoto via Getty Images Ukrainian special forces operating inside the kill zone regularly carry pump-action shotguns to destroy Russian drones controlled by fiber-optic cables ; these types of drones are able to resist the signal jamming that can incapacitate radio-frequency systems. Within the kill zone , which Ukrainian officials and soldiers say is expanding, troops often dismount and leave their vehicles behind to hike for miles, disperse to put distance between troops to avoid creating large targets, and increasingly rely on uncrewed tools like ground robots for logistics and casualty evacuation. The overwhelming presence of new military technology inside the kill zone underscores how much the conflict has changed since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Ukraine's defense ministry said earlier this month that drones now account for roughly 90% of all strikes, a dramatic shift in a war that was once primarily a grinding artillery battle . NATO, facing what military leadership has described as a worsening Russian threat , is increasingly looking to Ukraine for lessons on how to fight on a modern battlefield, one where small explosive-laden quadcopters hunt front-line infantry and drone boats engage combat air patrols. Grynkewich pointed out that NATO runs "a number of exercises where we'll even have Ukrainians come out and be opposition forces for us." He said that's helped sharpen NATO's ability to fight the wars of the future. "When they do that, day-one performance might not be so great, but by day six or seven, the soldiers of the alliance are right up on top on speed, and learning exactly what they need to learn," he said. NATO forces are learning lessons from Ukraine, even deploying systems proven in combat. US Army photo In March, for example, a Ukrainian-led opposition team used drones to defeat a NATO force in a naval combat drill off the coast of Portugal. The scenario fell under a larger exercise, which NATO said helped it train to use and defend against the threat of uncrewed surface vessels . French Adm. Pierre Vandier, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Transformation , said such exercises are a net positive for the alliance. "I think we achieved something great there, because now that has triggered a sort of awakening," he told Business Insider. Vandier, NATO's other strategic commander, oversees alliance modernization efforts . He said he believes Ukraine's participation makes the alliance a better fighting force. NATO forces have incorporated similar lessons from Ukraine into their training and doctrine, and in some cases, fielded battlefield-proven weapons such as the Merops counter-drone system , which the US rushed to the Middle East at the start of the Iran war . NATO officials are also absorbing war lessons through other initiatives, such as the Joint Analysis Training and Education Centre, JATEC, a program that uses real-time data from the conflict in Ukraine to inform allied defense planning. Military officials directly involved in JATEC told Business Insider last year that the program is mutually beneficial; NATO helps Ukraine address some of the war's most pressing issues , while Kyiv shares its battlefield experience with allies. It secured the top spot because it can genuinely replace your full-sized oven for family dinners and batch cooking without sacrificing precise temperature control or causing your kitchen to overheat. While the Ninja toaster oven handles most daily cooking tasks well, it won't replace your full-sized oven for big roasts. Plus, air fryer toaster ovens don't compare to the classic basket air fryers when it comes to cooking speed. If you're just cooking for one or two people and don't need the capacity of a toaster oven, check out our guide to the best air fryers for recommendations. Learn more about how Business Insider Reviews tests and researches kitchen products . Getting started Setting up the Ninja Foodi XL Pro is a breeze. All you need to do is unbox it, plug it in, and choose a cooking function. The interface is clearly labeled so you can adjust the time and temperature or scroll through the 10 presets. I especially liked that I could get it up and running without any mis-presses, a testament to the thoughtful design. One pro tip from extensive appliance testing : operate the unit empty at maximum temperature for at least 10 minutes before first use to eliminate the chemical odor common to new toaster ovens. This tempering of the appliance will ensure your food is untainted by ghastly aromas. Cooking performance Fries Making frozen fries is one of the most revealing tests for an air fryer toaster oven. James Brains/Business Insider The Ninja Foodi XL Pro took 18 minutes to turn frozen fries into fast-food-quality eats. The fries had a satisfying crispiness and a fluffy interior. The results were fairly uniform: no burned edges or underdone centers. Pizza We also made great frozen pizza in 12 minutes, which is about average for countertop ovens. The convection cooking created perfectly melted cheese and a beautifully crisp crust, though with too quick browning around the edges. The Ninja has an impressive capacity, accommodating two 12-inch pizzas. Chicken The Ninja Foodi XL Pro Air Fry Oven features a big front window and interior light, which make it easy to monitor food’s progress. James Brains/Business Insider The Ninja Foodi XL Pro did an outstanding job roasting a whole chicken, finishing a five-pound bird in 70 minutes — notably faster than most models. It cooked remarkably even throughout both white and dark meat portions. The finished chicken was textbook: impressive juiciness and perfectly crispy skin with consistent golden coloration. Most importantly, my family gobbled it up. Heating speed and consistency The Ninja Foodi XL Pro's preheating speeds were average: about eight minutes to reach 350 degrees Fahrenheit and just over nine to reach 425 degrees. However, it maintained precise temperatures. We set the oven to 350 degrees and measured the temperature every 15 minutes for two hours. The Ninja stayed between 349 and 352 degrees throughout our testing period, which is among the lowest variance we've seen. This precise temperature control makes the oven an excellent choice for following recipes and baking temperature-sensitive foods. Accessories, presets, and cleaning The Ninja Foodi XL Pro comes with an air fry basket, two wire racks, two sheet pans, and a roast tray. James Brains/Business Insider The Ninja Foodi XL Pro comes with two sheet pans and wire racks that allow you to cook multiple levels of food. The air fry basket is designed for maximum air circulation, and a dedicated roasting tray collects juices while preparing roasts. The oven has 10 preset cooking modes: whole roast, air roast, air fry, bake, dehydrate, broil, toast, pizza, and reheat. While most units only come with one wire rack, the Ninja has two, so you can dehydrate two layers of food simultaneously. Cleaning is mildly annoying. Only the air fry basket is dishwasher safe, and the remaining components should be washed by hand. The crumb tray is easily accessible to facilitate regular cleaning after every couple of uses, which we recommend to avoid grease buildup. Cons to consider Despite its impressive performance, the Ninja DT201 has a few drawbacks. It requires significant kitchen space — potentially problematic for space-starved apartments. Hand-washing most accessories (excluding the air fryer basket) is more time-consuming. I recommend placing your food on air fryer liners , foil, or parchment paper to speed up cleaning. The Ninja Foodi XL Pro is expensive for a toaster oven, retailing for $300, but we think the capacity and performance warrant the price. Plus, it's often marked down to $230 and sometimes as low as $200 on deal days. What are your alternatives? The Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is bigger than it looks, and has the most advanced heating technology on the market. Jennifer Zyman/Business Insider While the Ninja Foodi XL Pro is our best overall pick, it may not be right for every kitchen or home cook. Check out our guide to the best air fryer toaster ovens for more recommendations. If you're looking for a space-saving design , a different aesthetic, or specialized smart features, here's how Ninja compares to its closest rivals. Our pick Price Aesthetic and interface Best for Ninja Foodi XL Pro Air Fry oven $380 Industrial stainless steel with an integrated digital display handle. Large families and batch cooking for those who need a true full-size oven replacement. Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro $400 Premium brushed stainless steel with an LCD display and traditional dials. Home chefs who want sophisticated heating technology and high-end build quality. Café Couture Oven with Air Fry $449 Matte finishes with signature copper accents and digital LCD controls. Tech-savvy users who want a stunning aesthetic and smart home connectivity. Ninja Digital Air Fry Countertop Oven $450 Stainless steel, low-profile design with a digital control panel. Small kitchens and those who want an oven without sacrificing permanent counter space or installation. The precision rival: If you want (arguably) the most sophisticated heating technology on the market, the Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is a stellar choice. Powered by Breville's intelligent Element iQ system, it delivers exceptionally even heat to eliminate cold spots. It features 11 versatile cooking functions and a brushed stainless steel design, though you will be trading some of the Ninja's vertical interior capacity for Breville's premium build quality. The smart tech rival: If you love connected appliances and kitchen aesthetics are important to you, the Café Couture Oven with Air Fry is a gorgeous, high-tech alternative. Finished in bold matte colors with the brand's signature copper accents, it boasts 14 cooking modes and built-in WiFi. You can even use voice control via Amazon Echo or Google Home, and program recipes using the SmartHQ app. The space-saving rival: If you have limited counter space but still want the versatility of an oven, the Ninja Digital Air Fry Countertop Oven is a fantastic alternative. The clever, low-profile design flips up and stores vertically against your backsplash when not in use, making it space-efficient while still managing to fit a 13-inch pizza or nine slices of toast. Is Ninja a good brand? If you love the reliability and multi-functional performance of the brand's countertop ovens, we recommend checking out the rest of Ninja's product ecosystem . The brand consistently excels at packing professional-grade power and intuitive Auto-iQ technology into countertop appliances that simplify everyday cooking and prep. Here are some of the Ninja brand kitchen appliance and products we have tested and recommend. The bottom line My full-size oven got lonely while I was testing the Ninja Foodi XL Pro. I could cook everything in this toaster oven without consuming as much energy or putting out as much heat. It's your best bet when you don't have room for a standard oven, or you want an extra appliance for cooking sides when entertaining. Read the original article on Business Insider

title: Should You Buy SpaceX Stock Before Aug. 4?
content: Key Points SpaceX operates in the space transportation, satellite internet connectivity, and AI infrastructure industries. Its stock went public on June 12, and it has already plummeted by 45% from its peak. SpaceX will release its second-quarter operating results on Aug. 4, but even an extremely positive report might not be enough to turn its stock around. 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies › Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) went public on June 12, and it quickly soared to a peak of $225.64. However, it has since lost 45% of its value, so even investors who bought it at the official initial public offering (IPO) price of $135 are currently underwater. SpaceX is scheduled to release its operating results for the second quarter of 2026 (ended June 30) on Aug. 4. The report, and the accompanying conference call with CEO Elon Musk, will provide investors with an update on the company's space transportation, satellite internet connectivity, and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure businesses. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » However, a positive second-quarter report probably won't be enough to spark a recovery in SpaceX stock because of its sky-high valuation. Here's why buying it ahead of Aug. 4 might not be a good move. Image source: Getty Images. What Wall Street might be looking for on Aug. 4 SpaceX generated $4.7 billion in total revenue during the first quarter of 2026 (ended March 31), and here was the contribution from each of its three core segments: Segment First-Quarter Revenue Connectivity $3.26 billion AI $820 million Space $620 million Data source: SpaceX. Connectivity was the biggest source of revenue by far. SpaceX has used its Falcon 9 reusable rockets to launch over 9,600 Starlink satellites into orbit, which provide internet access to 10.3 million paying customers. The upcoming V3 Starlink satellites will deliver 10 times more bandwidth than the current V2 satellites, so they could give this business a huge boost when they start launching later this year. According to Yahoo! Finance, Wall Street analysts estimate SpaceX generated around $6.87 billion in total revenue during the second quarter, but I think the contributions from its three segments were probably vastly different compared to the first quarter. Connectivity was almost certainly a key source of revenue yet again, but the AI business likely showed substantial growth. In January, SpaceX acquired Elon Musk's AI start-up xAI, which operates enormous data centers like Colossus and Colossus II. This infrastructure is used to develop AI products like the Grok chatbot, but SpaceX is now renting some of the spare computing capacity to other companies in exchange for massive fees. In May, SpaceX agreed to rent $1.25 billion worth of computing capacity per month to Anthropic . In June, the company signed two more deals: one to rent $920 million worth of capacity per month to Google parent Alphabet starting in October, and another to rent $150 million worth of capacity per month to Reflection AI. As a result, revenue from the AI business likely surged in the second quarter compared to the first quarter, which is something Wall Street analysts might hang their hats on to justify SpaceX's hefty valuation. A positive quarterly report might not turn SpaceX stock around Despite the recent decline in SpaceX stock, it's still trading at a steep premium to the broader market. Its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 83.7 is more than 13 times higher than the P/S ratio of the Nasdaq-100 index, which is currently 6.2. In other words, SpaceX stock appears to be heavily overvalued relative to a basket of its big-tech peers. One single quarterly report is unlikely to show enough growth to make the stock look attractive at the current price. In fact, even if we use Wall Street's 2027 revenue estimate of $72.3 billion, SpaceX has a forward P/S ratio of 23.3, which is still very expensive compared to the Nasdaq-100. As a result, investors who buy this stock today need to have a very long-term time horizon of at least five years to give the company time to grow into its valuation. There is every chance it will eventually do so, because management believes its addressable market is worth $28.5 trillion across all three of its businesses. The AI infrastructure market alone could be worth $26.5 trillion. In the future, Elon Musk thinks SpaceX can launch computing clusters into orbit, where they will run on solar power and won't need complex cooling systems. Starlink satellites can beam the data down to Earth, so the company already has distribution sorted, giving it a huge advantage over any potential competitors. With all of that said, I wouldn't be piling into SpaceX stock ahead of its Aug. 4 report in the hope an immediate recovery will follow. This is very much a long-term story. title: I went inside the hidden Cadillac Club at Citi Field. It's the most exclusive place to watch the Mets play.
content: I toured the exclusive Cadillac Club at Citi Field to see what the members-only experience, field-level seats, and complimentary food are really like. Erin McDowell/Business Insider I toured Citi Field's hidden, members-only Cadillac Club. The club offers complimentary food and drinks, along with luxury seating. The setting was perfect for an avid baseball fan or someone wanting to experience the game in style. Luxury suites have become a major part of the modern ballpark experience, but few are as exclusive as the Cadillac Club at Citi Field. Hidden behind a members-only entrance near the players' tunnel, the speakeasy-inspired space offers complimentary food and drinks, a rotating chef-designed menu, and plush leather field-level seats just feet from right field. When the 100-seat club opened in 2023, access was initially available only through full-season club memberships, with first-row memberships costing $24,999 per seat, the Associated Press reported at the time. Last year, access expanded to some group sales, and more recently, "an extremely limited number of single game tickets" have been available for certain games, a spokesperson told Business Insider. Single-game seats are also being sold on third-party websites. As of July 22, third-row seats in the Cadillac Club for the Mets' July 25 game against the Los Angeles Dodgers were listed for $688 each. On a recent gameday between the Mets and Kansas City Royals, I was granted access to the Cadillac Club as a member of the press, eager to see whether the experience lived up to the hype — and prices. Here's what it's like inside one of baseball's most exclusive clubs. On a recent gameday against the Kansas City Royals, I went inside the Cadillac Club. Erin McDowell/Business Insider The Cadillac Club at Payson's is one of the most exclusive places to watch a Mets game at Citi Field. The stadium, which opened in 2009 to replace Shea Stadium, blends modern amenities with tributes to the Mets' history, including the Jackie Robinson Rotunda and architectural nods to Brooklyn's historic Ebbets Field. In recent years, Citi Field has added premium clubs and hospitality spaces, including the Cadillac Club, which opened in 2023. The trend is playing out across ballparks and arenas as teams look to boost revenue and attract corporate clients and wealthy fans seeking more exclusive experiences. In 2025, Rocket Arena, home to the NBA's Cleveland Cavaliers, opened HIPP, an invitation-only members club. Access was initially offered only to fans who had already spent at least $100,000 with the team, The New York Times reported. That same year, Capital One Arena in Washington, DC — home to the NBA's Wizards and the NHL's Capitals — debuted six high-end, private suites, each costing more than $1 million a year to lease. Even the entrance felt exclusive. Erin McDowell/Business Insider Unlike most premium seating areas, the Cadillac Club isn't immediately visible. Thankfully, I had been given directions on where to go. After entering Citi Field, I headed for a discreet entrance that led me away from the crowds and toward a hallway near the players' tunnel. The club itself wasn't listed on any of the signs I saw outside the stadium. Since it's marketed as a speakeasy, only those with directions would know how to access it. The entrance to the Cadillac Club features Mets memorabilia and a hidden door. Erin McDowell/Business Insider However, before I reached the club itself, I stepped into a hallway lined with framed photographs, vintage memorabilia, and televisions showing the game. At first glance, it looked like a cozy lounge celebrating the team's history … until I realized one of the paintings concealed the hidden entrance to the Cadillac Club. To enter, I had to say "Let's go, Mets!" and the door opened — a fun touch that added an element of magic to the experience. The club is named after one of the Mets' most important figures. Erin McDowell/Business Insider The Cadillac Club honors Joan Whitney Payson, the Mets' founding principal owner and the first woman to independently purchase a majority ownership stake in a Major League Baseball team. She maintained ownership from the Mets' founding in 1960 until her death in 1975. When I finally reached the entrance, I thought it looked more like the gateway to a secret garden than a baseball stadium. Erin McDowell/Business Insider The entrance, framed in greenery, was manned by security personnel, who scanned tickets to ensure the club's exclusivity. In addition to club access, the Cadillac Club membership includes private restrooms, VIP reserved parking in Official Lot A, a dedicated premium experience manager, and exclusive member events. Once inside, I almost forgot I was at Citi Field. Erin McDowell/Business Insider It was a particularly humid day in New York City, so I was glad for the respite inside the exclusive, climate-controlled area, rather than sweating up in the nosebleed seats as I typically would. Warm wood finishes, leather seating, and a bar lining the entire back wall of the 7,000-square-foot space made the club feel more like an upscale New York restaurant or bar than a sports venue. Greenery was also woven throughout the space. Erin McDowell/Business Insider Gensler, one of the world's biggest architecture firms, designed the speakeasy. Combined with the leather seating and warm lighting, large trees and hanging plants created a cozy, secluded atmosphere that lived up to its speakeasy inspiration. The bar was stocked with beer, wine, and spirits. Erin McDowell/Business Insider Members receive complimentary soft drinks, beer, and wine throughout the game, while premium liquor and cocktails are also available for purchase. There was plenty of space to grab a drink without having to fight long concession lines. The private bar area felt buzzy without being overly crowded. Screens along the bar also meant guests never missed a moment of the game while ordering, eating, or drinking. The seats were, unsurprisingly, the biggest draw of watching from inside the Cadillac Club. Erin McDowell/Business Insider Leather armchairs, which come with personal flat-screen monitors, are assigned to members for the season. They were located just feet from right field, with an open-air design that let a breeze flow in from the warning track. Being so close to the players made every pitch, hit, and catch feel much more immersive than watching from higher up in the stadium . The view of the field was mostly unobstructed, and while I could hear noise from the stands, it was more a steady stream of chatter than a roar. I loved being able to move between the game and the lounge area. Erin McDowell/Business Insider Unlike traditional seating, the Cadillac Club encourages guests to wander between the seats and the indoor lounge, where they can still catch the game. "This stadium is designed more along the lines of a resort," executive chef Jason Eksterowicz, who spent much of his career at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas before joining Citi Field in 2017, told me. "Instead of a big pool, it's a baseball field." Another draw of watching the game from the Cadillac Club is the all-you-can-eat buffet. Erin McDowell/Business Insider In the "ballpark classics" section of the buffet, options included Bavarian pretzel sticks, crinkle-cut fries, and crispy chicken tenders, served with dipping sauces such as ketchup, honey mustard, and ranch. Members and their guests also have access to more refined offerings than the typical stadium fare. The rotating buffet includes multiple hot entrées, salads, and sides. "A lot of the flavor profiles and foods you're going to find in our stadium are traditional flavors that everyone can relate to, maybe presented and mashed up in a unique way," Eksterowicz said. The Cadillac Club doesn't serve the same buffet every game. Erin McDowell/Business Insider Eksterowicz said the culinary team rotates roughly 25 to 30 menus, meaning that even season-ticket holders who attend games throughout the season rarely see the same spread more than a few times. "We want something that's going to be fresh. We want something that's going to be fast. We don't want anyone to miss an important part of the game," he said. Of course, there were classic ballpark hot dogs. Erin McDowell/Business Insider No Mets game would feel complete without hot dogs. The club served grilled dogs with traditional toppings like ketchup, mustard, and sauerkraut. When food started to run out, servers topped up the platters. There were also healthier options, such as a beet, arugula, and goat cheese salad. Erin McDowell/Business Insider It balanced out some of the richer comfort food elsewhere on the buffet. The dessert station included an assortment of cookies in several flavors. Erin McDowell/Business Insider The red velvet cookie especially caught my eye. In addition to the buffet, the club also provides classic baseball snacks. Erin McDowell/Business Insider The club offered complimentary nostalgic snacks, from Cracker Jack to peanuts, throughout the game. The Cadillac Club struck a great balance between luxury hospitality and a genuine baseball atmosphere. Erin McDowell/Business Insider Before visiting, I assumed the biggest draw would be sitting just a few feet from the field. However, the whole experience impressed me. From its hidden entrance and upscale interiors, its rotating chef-designed menus and complimentary food and drinks, the Cadillac Club delivered an experience that went far beyond typical ballpark food and a standard seat. With an exclusive atmosphere that at times felt more like a high-end restaurant than a stadium club, I can see the draw for high-net-worth fans and business clients. As someone who isn't a major baseball fan, I personally wouldn't buy a full-season membership. Still, when I checked a ticket resale website, some tickets appeared to be around $400 to $500, a price I could see myself paying for access to the Cadillac Club. The food, drinks, atmosphere, premium amenities, and location right on the field made it feel like the only way to spend a day out at the ballgame. Read the original article on Business Insider

title: Top US general says Ukraine's F-16s recently shot down their first Russian fighter jet, showing how far its air defense has come
content: Gen. Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said Ukraine had its first air-to-air kill with an F-16. Vitalii Nosach/Global Images Ukraine via Getty Images A top US general said a Ukrainian F-16 scored the country's first air-to-air kill. He said it showed how far Ukraine's layered defenses have developed. The general did not specify what kind of Russian fighter jet was shot down in the engagement. Ukraine's F-16 fighter jets scored their first air-to-air kill by shooting down a Russian fighter jet, a top US general said, calling the engagement a sign of Ukraine's improving air defenses. US Air Force Gen. Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said during a congressional hearing on Tuesday that "recently we had the first air-to-air kill where a Ukrainian F-16 shot down a Russian fighter." He described it as evidence of Ukraine's growing air-defense capability. "I think their ability to scale their layered defense has come a long way over the last couple years with the help and assistance of many," he said at a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing. An effective layered defense employs different sensors and weapons, positioned at varying distances and altitudes, to counter varied threats. It requires not only having enough sensors and weapons fielded, but also the ability to connect them, share information, and assign the right weapon to each threat. Ukraine has expanded those defenses during Russia's full-scale invasion, combining domestically developed technology and Western weapons with Soviet-era systems already in service. Caine did not provide details about the engagement, including where it occurred or what type of Russian aircraft was shot down. Some observers have speculated that he may have been referring to a July 8 Ukrainian Air Force claim that its forces downed a Russian Su-35. That, however, remains unclear. The general cited the growth of Ukraine's defense industry and said he wanted to "highlight the incredible work that the Ukraine industrial base is doing as they scale their own capabilities. It ranges from their surface-to-air capabilities to their air-to-air capabilities." He was speaking in response to a question about what impact a potential US halting of air defense funding to Ukraine for three years would have. Though it has significantly improved its defenses since the start of the war, including through domestic developments such as interceptor drones, Ukraine continues to ask for any and all air defense support it can get as Russian drone and missile bombardments worsen and continue to threaten both military and civilian infrastructure. Ukraine received its first batch of F-16s in summer 2024 after a long debate among Western militaries about whether the provision of these fighter jets could be perceived as unnecessarily escalatory and how quickly Ukraine could integrate them and build the training, maintenance, logistics, and operational systems needed to use them effectively. Ukraine has managed to integrate these assets into its air force, using them to intercept Russian drones and missiles, conduct strikes on ground targets, and now engage hostile crewed aircraft. And Western partner nations are now studying how Ukraine combines cheap sensors , interceptor drones, dispersed operations, and older flying techniques to strengthen its air defenses and operations. Partner nations are providing other advanced Western jets to Ukraine, including Swedish Gripens and French Mirages, framing it as both the result of Ukraine's competency and allied desire to integrate Ukraine into the future of Western defense, not just to have it survive this war. title: Elon Musk's posts about making an espresso in FSD are being scrutinized in a Tesla investigation
content: "Make your espresso on the road while your Tesla drives itself," wrote Musk in one post. Johannes Neudecker/picture alliance via Getty Images Elon Musk's X posts are putting Tesla in hot water with regulators, again. Regulators asked Tesla for more information about Musk's posts that FSD users could text and make espressos while driving. It's not the first time the company has faced scrutiny over the way it promotes its Full Self-Driving tech. Elon Musk's posting habits are putting Tesla under the microscope — again . Regulators looking into Tesla's Full Self-Driving have asked the company for more information about a series of X posts in which CEO Elon Musk said drivers could text and make an espresso while using the automated driving assist technology. In a request for information sent to Tesla on July 2, officials at the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) asked the company to clarify posts made on Musk and Tesla's accounts. These include a post from December 2025 in which Musk said FSD users could text and drive "depending on [the] context of surrounding traffic." "This is so cool. Make your espresso on the road while your Tesla drives itself," Musk wrote in another post cited by the document. The billionaire was responding to a video showing a Tesla owner using an espresso machine and reclining his seat while FSD was engaged. The NHTSA also cited posts from Musk saying that FSD can "operate in all conditions" and that an FSD update will "substantially reduce" the need for driver attention, as well as posts from Tesla promoting the technology. The regulator asked Tesla to clarify whether these examples were "accurate and consistent" with FSD's capabilities, and if the company has done anything to reduce the potential for "misunderstanding or misuse." On its website and in owner manuals , Tesla makes it clear that drivers using Full Self-Driving (Supervised) should pay attention to the road and be ready to take over at all times. It's not the first time Tesla has faced legal and regulatory scrutiny over the way it promotes FSD. The Model Y maker was ordered to pay $242 million in damages last year over a wrongful-death lawsuit that alleged Tesla's advertising exaggerated the capabilities of Autopilot, FSD's predecessor, and the company struck a deal to avoid a ban in California in February after a judge ruled that its "Autopilot" and "Full Self-Driving" branding was misleading. The NHTSA investigation, which was opened in October 2024 and upgraded to an engineering analysis in March, is looking into FSD's ability to alert the driver in low-visibility conditions. The probe was opened following several reports of Tesla's crashing in areas where visibility was reduced by "sun glare, fog, or airborne dust." Tesla did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Read the original article on Business Insider

title: 3 Dividend Stocks Built for Long-Term Buy-and-Hold Investors
content: Key Points Chevron is an energy giant and has lifted its annual dividend for 39 consecutive years. ExxonMobil is the U.S.'s largest oil producer and the world's largest non-state-owned refiner. Enbridge's tollbooth-like business insulates it from fluctuating oil prices. 10 stocks we like better than Chevron › It's always nice to see your stocks appreciate, but that's far from the only way to make money in the stock market. Plenty of investors build a lot of wealth over time by embracing dividend stocks and leaning on the guaranteed income they (typically) provide. Much of the value from investing comes over time, but it's especially true for dividend investors because dividends take time to compound. If you're looking for three dividend stocks you can confidently buy and hold for the long haul, look no further than Chevron (NYSE: CVX), ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM), and Enbridge (NYSE: ENB). They are three energy stocks with longevity you don't have to question. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Image source: Getty Images. Chevron has a hand in many different energy pots Chevron is one of the world's largest fully integrated energy companies. It finds and extracts its own crude oil (upstream), transports and stores oil and gas (midstream), and makes final products like gasoline and diesel that people use every day (downstream). Each segment has its own set of pluses and risks, so having a hand in all three helps keep the business stable when different segments are in different parts of a cycle. That's why Chevron has consistently been one of the go-to dividend stocks in the energy sector. When Chevron announced a dividend increase earlier this year, it was the 39th consecutive year that it had done so. It's not Dividend King status (a company with 50-plus years of consecutive increases), but it would be very surprising if it doesn't hit that mark in 11 years. Chevron also has the financials (and financial discipline) that should make investors comfortable holding the stock without thinking twice. This year, it will pay out around $14 billion in dividends, less than the free cash flow it's expected to generate. ExxonMobil's scale is a competitive advantage ExxonMobil is the largest oil company in the U.S., both in market value ($610 billion at the time of writing) and oil production. It also has upstream, midstream, and downstream operations, but what primarily sets it apart from Chevron is its footprint and focus. Chevron's key asset is the U.S. Permian Basin, the country's largest oil-producing region, located in western Texas and parts of New Mexico. ExxonMobil's key asset is the offshore Guyana territory it operates in. ExxonMobil also focuses much more on the downstream segment, as the world's largest non-state-owned refiner. The differences mean you can own both without feeling like there's too much overlap between them. ExxonMobil has the lowest dividend yield among the three companies (around 2.8%), but it has produced the best total returns over the past five years by a long shot because of its stock price growth. Its focus on high-return projects and large acquisitions (such as its $64.5 billion acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources) has attracted investors who prefer ExxonMobil's more aggressive growth plan. Its sheer scale makes it a great dividend stock to hold on to for decades. Enbridge is the tollbooth that keeps getting more lucrative Enbridge is more of a pure-play energy company, only operating in the midstream. It's a Canadian company that owns one of the largest pipeline networks around. It serves over 75% of North American oil refineries and transports a fifth of all of North America's natural gas. Enbridge's business is essentially a tollbooth. It charges volume-based or fixed fees to transport products through its pipelines and other infrastructure. Some contracts may be long-term, while others are per-service, but either way, it's insulated from price fluctuations. It doesn't matter if a barrel of crude oil is $50 or $100; Enbridge collects the same fees. Enbridge's current dividend yield is 4.9%, which is attractive, but noticeably below the 6.4% it has averaged over the past three years. However, that's because of its stock price growth rather than a drop in its dividend. It has 31 consecutive years of dividend increases. It would be extremely hard for competitors to replicate Enbridge's footprint . The regulatory and financial barriers give Enbridge a competitive moat that ensures longevity. It will continue being one of the more dominant midstream energy companies for quite some time. Should you buy stock in Chevron right now? title: Hyperscalers Can Make/Break This Market
Dynavox Group AB (publ) (TDVXF) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
Tech's AI debt boom, in one chart
content: The year of tech companies tapping the debt markets to fuel their AI ambitions is far from over, and debt issuance is already busting through Wall Street projections, with five months left to go in 2026. Quick insight: The numbers surrounding 2026 debt issuance border on mind-blowing. In a new research note from Goldman Sachs strategist Amanda Lynam on Wednesday, she estimated that $489 billion of AI-related debt has been issued this year. That's already above Goldman's estimate of $322 billion for how much of this debt came to market last year. About 40% of this year's AI-related debt supply has been issued directly by hyperscalers. Data center financing and other parts of the tech ecosystem have also contributed. The year of AI debt. · Goldman Sachs This year, Amazon ( AMZN ) has raised about $53 billion in debt, including a $37 billion US bond offering and more than $16 billion in euro-denominated bonds. Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) has issued roughly $20 billion in bonds. Oracle ( ORCL ) has raised about $25 billion to fund its aggressive AI expansion. Meta ( META ) has also tapped debt markets in a big way, following its roughly $30 billion bond offering late last year with additional financing tied to AI infrastructure projects. "We expect a range of financing markets will ultimately be required to satisfy the multi-year funding needs related to the AI build-out," Lynam explained. "This includes various parts of the syndicated credit markets (investment grade, high yield, loans), the private markets (especially infrastructure), new 'project finance' style joint venture structures, and various regional bond markets (across currencies). For example, we estimate nearly $200 billion of data center deals have been completed in the private markets — across all categories — since early 2025." Big Tech is about to spend trillions to dominate the AI era Tech giants are not going to slash their AI spending: Analyst Alphabet's $80 billion stock sale shows how expensive AI is getting An AlphaSpace case study: Arguably, nowhere has the AI debt-issuance boom reshaped a tech balance sheet more than at Oracle ( ORCL ). Billionaire Larry Ellison's tech giant ended its recent fiscal year with $149 billion in long-term debt, up sharply from $96 billion in the prior fiscal year, according to Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data. The company ended its fiscal year with $31.3 billion in total cash. The company's rising debt position is one reason the stock has crashed more than 50% from June 2. "I'll tell you there's big execution risk," BD8 Capital Partners CEO and chief investment officer Barbara Doran said on Yahoo Finance's Opening Bid (see video above). "I mean, there's no question they have a huge backlog, although there is big customer concentration risk there. But it's really the debt issue, as we know. And S&P just downgraded to triple B minus. That is one notch above junk status. And so they're really betting the house on this continued demand and the fact that there is plenty of room for more capacity to be added, but it's going to take time." Story Continues The bottom line: At the moment, markets are handling the additional debt being tacked onto tech companies in stride, as many have the cash flow generation to support the leverage. But a day of reckoning could come in 2027 if signs emerge that AI monetization is not living up to the hype. Several interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve would also be a headwind. title: Unique watches to buy if you want a luxury timepiece that stands out from the crowd
content: A frosted Royal Oak mini from Audemars Piguet. Moritz Scholz/Getty Images The watch industry is full of unique and coveted wrist candy. You've probably seen or heard about popular options from Patek Philippe, Cartier, and more. If you want to stand out, though, consider watches from F.P.Journe, Daniel Roth, and Gérald Genta. If you're wearing a Cartier or Patek Phillipe watch while reading this, congratulations! You've secured a timepiece from one of the most coveted brands on the market. Many of us, though, have yet to secure that kind of wrist candy. Buying luxury watches isn't as easy as going to the store and picking one out. Many brands require you to shop around boutiques, join waitlists, and sometimes, revert to shopping secondhand. And that's not to mention how difficult it can be to choose a model that speaks to you. For those having trouble, we can help. In an interview with Business Insider, Quaid Walker, the CEO of the watch marketplace Bezel , shared the timepieces he thinks will make anyone stand out in a crowd — even when the most coveted pieces are around. Anything from A. Lange & Söhne will catch the attention of fellow watch lovers. A watch from A. Lange & Söhne. Fabrice Coffrini/Getty Images Walker described the German watchmaker as an "incredible brand that has repeatedly gone up in value, in a way that has even surprised huge watch fans ." "The market wants something that feels different and interesting, and it's driving folks to models like [those from A. Lange & Söhne]," he said. Some watches from the brand cost upward of $49,500, though many are listed on the A. Lange & Söhne website as "price upon request." Models like the Zeitwerk watch are coveted and can cost close to $100,000. Cartier Panthère models are everywhere, but a mini frosted Royal Oak might get more attention. Moritz Scholz/Getty Images These days, you'd struggle to find an it-girl influencer or celebrity who hasn't sported a Cartier Panthère . It's undoubtedly become the queen of small watches, which have been trending for men and women lately. Still, it's not the only option out there. "Tastemakers have really shifted things," Walker said. "If you see your favorite celebrity walk down the red carpet wearing [a frosted Royal Oak], you might say, 'I want that. It's different from a standard Panthère.'" Of course, Audemars Piguet timepieces are known for their higher price points. Frosted Royal Oaks are no exception. The mini models retail for $41,100, and the larger sizes can cost upward of $74,000 . Many people love F.P.Journe, but there's more to the brand than the Chronomètre Bleu. A selection of F.P.Journe watches. Fabrice Coffrini/Getty Images F.P.Journe is beloved by watch collectors like Mark Zuckerberg . Still, interest is rising in some of the brand's hard-to-find designs. "There are certain F.P.Journes that, maybe three years ago, were selling between $30,000 and $50,000," Walker said. "They're now selling between $150,000 to $200,000." That's because production of the brand's designs is limited. If you find one, you instantly gain the status of a serious watch collector. "Wearing a certain Journe is like what wearing a Nautilus [used to be]," he added, comparing the brand to one of Patek Philippe's most famed and coveted designs. To stand out, Walker recommends looking into F.P.Journe's Élégante watch , which can sell for about $125,000, or the brand's Chronomètre Optimum , which can cost more than $500,000. If you can't secure an F.P.Journe, you should turn to watchmakers that in-the-know fans love, like Daniel Roth. Two watches from Daniel Roth. Daniel Roth Daniel Roth is a Swiss luxury watch brand founded in 1988. It temporarily halted production in 2015 but was revived in 2023. Walker recommends two unique models from the brand: the Tourbillion Platinum and the Extra Plat . The latter are listed on Bezel for more than $73,000, while the former can cost over $200,000 on the secondhand market. Gérald Genta and Breguet are also brands to consider. A Breguet Tradition watch. Bloomberg/Getty Images Both brands are from Switzerland and have left major marks on the watch industry. Gérald Genta is known as the "Picasso of watches," in part for his invention of luxury sports watches, and Breguet is known as the "godfather of watchmaking," having been founded in 1775. Walker said that the former brand's vintage watches will make any wearer stand out. The $15,000 Donald Duck watch is just one option. When it comes to Breguet, he recommends the $36,185 Tradition 7057 and the $49,325 vintage Classique Perpetual Calendar . Read the original article on Business Insider

title: Mamdani throws business leaders a curveball: Tapping antitrust crusader Lina Khan
content: Former Federal Trade Commission Chair Lina Khan will head the board of directors for NYC's Economic Development Corporation. Alexi J. Rosenfeld/Getty Images Longtime Mamdani ally Lina Khan will head the board of directors for NYC economic development. McKinsey partner and former public servant, Anthony Shorris, will take on the president role. The mayor hopes to marry his affordability goals with ongoing business development in the city. Zohran Mamdani has tapped Lina Khan — a longtime ally and co-chair of his mayoral transition — to lead the board of directors for New York City's Economic Development Corporation. The mayor announced Khan's role in the City Hall Rotunda on Wednesday morning. McKinsey partner Anthony Shorris will join her as president and CEO of the EDC. Mamdani called the pair "a dream team" — a move he hopes is good news for both business growth and his affordability agenda . "Today's appointees not only share a vision for the future of this office, but a commitment too, to executing on it," the mayor said. He feels that both Khan and Shorris are aligned in thinking that the measure of a city's economic strength is "whether it is able to lift up those who are currently priced out." Khan added that the "EDC has key tools to drive projects that grow our economy, create good jobs, promote entrepreneurship, and make life more affordable for New Yorkers." Khan could bring Mamdani's affordability goals to EDC The organization, a quasi-public nonprofit that manages city-owned property, works alongside the local government to support business interests and economic growth. It largely operates as its own entity, despite leadership traditionally being handpicked by the mayor. EDC can develop real estate, manage assets, award business incentives, and oversee major construction projects on behalf of the city. Besides playing a strategic role in the Mamdani campaign, Khan served as director of the Federal Trade Commission under President Joe Biden and has a reputation as an antitrust crusader and defender of consumer rights. She has accompanied the mayor and his cabinet to press events in recent months and served in a "voluntary advisor" role, her spokesperson Douglas Farrar told Business Insider, but this will be her first official job within the administration. The EDC leadership position has been a source of tension in City Hall since Mamdani began his term. Some civic leaders have said it is unusual that Mamdani took months to appoint a new head of the EDC. Critics said the delay indicated that business and tech investment aren't a priority for the mayor , who has been vocal about his affordability platform for lower- and middle-income New Yorkers and has been tough on corporations. The appointment of Khan alongside Shorris — who has had a decadeslong career in public service and the private sector — is an effort to marry these development and cost-of-living goals, Mamdani said. Shorris, for example, had a role in establishing the minimum wage and universal 3-K programs in NYC, and previously led the New York-New Jersey Port Authority. "As City Hall takes on the affordability crisis gripping our city," he said. "As we work to reimagine economic models that give so much to so few — and deny so many others the basics of a dignified life — we believe that economic development and economic justice must go hand in hand." title: The 1 ETF I'd Buy if I Could Only Own One
content: Key Points The Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) invests in roughly 3,500 U.S. stocks, making it one of the best diversified, low-cost investments available. I prefer the VTI over the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) because of its 10%-15% allocation to mid-cap and small-cap stocks. With the small-cap earnings outlook significantly improving, this could be the catalyst that turns VTI into an outperformer. 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF › If I could only own one ETF right now, I'd buy the Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (NYSEMKT: VTI). By owning roughly 3,500 U.S. stocks, it's one of the most diverse ETFs you'll find. It's the ideal foundation for building the rest of your portfolio. And with an expense ratio of just 0.03%, it costs almost nothing to own it. Why choose a total stock market ETF over the S&P 500? The biggest selling point for this fund, in my opinion, is that it targets the entire investable U.S. stock market. A lot of people will use something like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO) for this purpose. I don't blame them, and it's a perfectly reasonable choice for a portfolio centerpiece. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Image source: Getty Images. But I prefer the Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF's all-cap approach versus the S&P 500 's large-cap focus. Mid-cap and small-cap stocks only make up around 10% to 15% of the portfolio overall, but it's important to include them. Smaller companies have historically experienced extended periods of outperformance relative to large caps, and investors should want that in their portfolios. Plus, the Vanguard Russell 2000 ETF (NASDAQ: VTWO), a proxy for small-caps, has a much different sector composition than the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF . That diversification can also help smooth out the ride in the long term. The S&P 500 is as top-heavy as it's ever been right now. The Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF isn't much better because it also weights by market cap, but it offers better diversification. Why VTI is a better choice than VOO for your portfolio right now Small-cap performance has clearly been an anchor on total stock market ETFs for several years. That's largely been a function of this group's relatively poor financial performance. Earnings growth for small-caps had been minimal at a time when large-cap earnings were still growing at a healthy rate. That's quickly becoming a thing of the past. Earnings growth for the S&P 600 Small Cap Index is expected to come in around 18% in 2026 and another 18% in 2027. That puts small-caps in a much healthier position today and could mean they finally take advantage of some of the relative value currently built into share prices. That puts all-cap funds like the Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF in a comparatively advantageous position for the first time in a while. That's why I believe this is the one fund to own both in the short-term and long-term. It won't always outperform, but its diversification, low cost, and ability to capture the entire market instead of just a subset are what set it apart. title: Anthropic is heating up the midterm proxy war over AI regulation
content: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei separately donated $1 million to a Super PAC allied with Public First Action. Chris Ratcliffe/Bloomberg/Getty Images Anthropic has doubled its commitment to a pro-AI regulations nonprofit. In total, the AI giant has spent $40 million ahead of November's midterm elections. The group Public First Action has clashed with a super PAC backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman. Anthropic is looking to throw its weight around ahead of this November's midterm elections. On Wednesday, Anthropic announced it is donating another $20 million to a nonprofit organization tied to three allied super PACs that have already supported Republican and Democratic candidates up and down the ballot. In total, Anthropic is set to spend $40 million to support the organization, Public First Action. "Our donation to Public First Action is one way in which we're trying to raise the salience of this urgent policy debate," Anthropic said in a statement. Anthropic said its push has only grown more urgent as AI models like Claude Mythos are developed. "We need policymakers and candidates to put forward measures that mitigate risks," the company said in the statement. Unlike super PACs, Public First Action is not required to disclose its donors. In June, the nonprofit said it had raised $80 million to date. Anthropic said its donation "cannot be used to influence the election of any candidate for federal, state, or local office," but the nonprofit can and has routed donations to advertising that highlights specific candidates. For example, Public First Action's first ad was focused on Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn's work on AI and child online safety legislation. Blackburn is leaving Congress in hopes of becoming Tennessee's next governor. Former Congressman Chris Stewart, a Republican from Utah, and Brad Carson, a Democrat from Oklahoma, cofounded Public First Action. Stewart and Carson have their own allied Super PACs that support Republican and Democratic candidates called "Defending Our Values PAC" and "Jobs and Democracy PAC." Public First Action, the Anthropic-backed group, has positioned itself in opposition to Leading the Future, a Super PAC funded by figures such as OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Marc Andreessen, and Ben Horowitz. OpenAI has said that Brockman is operating in his personal capacity in supporting the group, which has raised more than $75 million so far. While leading AI CEOs have increasingly called for some form of US-led regulation, none have been as outspoken or pushed for as stringent standards as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei . In an essay last month, Amodei said the government should create an agency akin to the Federal Aviation Administration, which governs air travel, to impose mandatory testing of certain advanced AI models and to block the release of an AI model if such evaluations raise red flags. The Trump administration and others in the AI industry have warned against such mandatory reviews. In May, Amodei separately donated $1 million to Public First, the only Super PAC allied with Public First Action that supports both Republicans and Democrats.
